title: Problem Overview
content:
**Erdős Problem #570: Cycle-Graph Ramsey Numbers**

For k ≥ 3 and H with m edges (no isolated vertices):
R(C_k, H) ≤ 2m + ⌈(k-1)/2⌉

**Status:** SOLVED (1993-2024)

The resolution required fundamentally different techniques for even and odd cycles, and spanned over 30 years from the original even-k proof to the final odd-k completion.
mathContext: R(G, H) is the minimum n such that any 2-coloring of K_n contains either G or H as a monochromatic subgraph.

title: Cycle Graph (Constructive)
content:
**CycleGraph k:** The cycle C_k on k vertices (k ≥ 3).

Adjacency: vertices i and j are adjacent iff j ≡ i+1 (mod k) or i ≡ j+1 (mod k).

This is one of the few constructive definitions in the file. The symmetry proof uses the disjunction structure of adjacency. The loopless proof shows (i+1) mod k ≠ i when k ≥ 3, using the fact that k ∤ 1.

This is the graph the 'red' player tries to find in the Ramsey game.
mathContext: $C_k$ has vertex set $\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ and edges $\{i, i+1\}$ for $i = 0, \ldots, k-1$. It is the unique 2-regular graph on $k$ vertices.

title: Edge Count and Isolated Vertices
content:
**edgeCount G:** Number of edges in graph G, computed as the cardinality of the edge set.

**NoIsolatedVertices G:** Every vertex has at least one neighbor. This condition ensures m ≥ |V(H)|/2, which is needed for the bound to be meaningful.

These predicates characterize the graph H in the conjecture statement.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of edge count and isolated vertices

title: Ramsey Number Definition
content:
**RamseyNumber G H:** The minimum n such that any 2-coloring of K_n contains either a red G or blue H.

Formalized as sInf of the set of valid n values. The CycleRamseyNumber specializes this to R(C_k, H).

**Ramsey's theorem** guarantees this infimum is over a non-empty set: R(G, H) always exists and is finite.
mathContext: Frank Ramsey proved the existence of these numbers in 1930. Computing exact values is notoriously difficult.

title: The Conjecture Statement
content:
**Erdos570Conjecture:**

∀ k ≥ 3, ∀ H with m edges and no isolated vertices:
R(C_k, H) ≤ 2m + ⌈(k-1)/2⌉

The **UpperBound function** computes 2m + ⌈(k-1)/2⌉ using natural number arithmetic. The bound is linear in m with a small additive correction depending on the cycle length k.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of the conjecture statement

title: Historical Case-by-Case Proofs
content:
**Four axioms covering all cases:**

1. **efrs_1993_even:** Even k ≥ 4 (Erdős-Faudree-Rousseau-Schelp, 1993)
2. **sidorenko_1993_triangle:** k = 3 (Sidorenko, 1993)
3. **jayawardene_1999_pentagon:** k = 5 (Jayawardene, 1999)
4. **cfmpp_2024_odd:** Odd k ≥ 7 (Cambie-Freschi-Morawski-Petrova-Pokrovskiy, 2024)

Together these cover all k ≥ 3. Even cycles use one technique; odd cycles required three separate proofs over 30 years.
mathContext: The even/odd distinction reflects structural differences in cycle embeddings and extremal graph theory.

title: Complete Resolution
content:
**erdos_570_resolved:** Erdos570Conjecture

The full conjecture is axiomatized as resolved. While the individual cases cover all k ≥ 3, combining them in Lean requires handling unbounded case analysis (all odd k ≥ 7), which is axiomatized rather than proved by tactic.

The key insight: even k handled by EFRS; odd k = 3 by Sidorenko; odd k = 5 by Jayawardene; odd k ≥ 7 by CFMPP.
